designSummary: Weekly time series: p-chart of returned referrals and run chart of median time to triage, with a twelve-week baseline and dated countermeasures.
sampleSize: The intake receives about 180 referrals a week. With a baseline of 22 percent, the p-chart's three-sigma limits sit about 9 percentage points either side of the centre line, so a sustained fall to 10 percent would show as a shift within a few weeks and single weeks below about 13 percent would signal special cause. Twelve baseline weeks give a stable centre line. The 20-referral weekly sample for bypass estimates a proportion of 25 percent with a 95 percent interval of about 19 points per week, so bypass is judged on four-week pooled samples.
primaryAnalysis: p-chart of weekly returned referrals with the baseline centre line and limits frozen after twelve weeks; shift, trend and point-outside-limits rules fixed before the redesign; limits recalculated only after a sustained shift.
secondaryAnalysis: Run chart of weekly median time to triage with the same rules; four-week pooled bypass proportions; descriptive practice timing; returned referrals by practice group.
missingData: Weeks with system outages are annotated and excluded from limit calculation, never imputed; missing bypass samples are recorded.
multiplicity: One primary measure; others are described with their charts and not tested.
software: Spreadsheet control chart template maintained with the lean coach.
overfittingGuards: Chart rules fixed before the redesign
Countermeasure dates marked before looking at the following weeks
No post hoc subgroup charts beyond the planned practice groups
summary: About 180 referrals a week make a p-chart sensitive to the targeted fall; bypass judged on pooled samples.
